We went to Vienna looking for its most famous schnitzel. Instead, we abandoned the queue and found our best one by accident. Our original plan was Figlmüller, where I had eaten years earlier. But the original location wasn’t accepting guests without a reservation—and its second restaurant had another long line outside. Across the street, Kussmaul was almost empty. Leaving Vienna’s most famous schnitzel queue for a quiet restaurant didn’t feel like the obvious decision. But the meat was incredibly tender, the coating was wonderfully crunchy, and it became our best Wienerschnitzel experience up to that point.
